founder_feedback.quote: The pages lack actual creative direction and coherence from Opus. Again, it’s just a bunch of text, so it feels exhausting going through all of it. Endless scrolling and whatnot.
answer: One composition per kind of work instead of one template for 504 pages: a truck (fleet), a month (bookkeeping), a calendar (compliance), a company (Client 360).
Desktop fits one screen; only lists scroll. Phone records open in a drawer instead of a 2,000 px page.
Detail on demand: one section at a time in a context panel, chosen from the work itself (a tag on the truck, a node on the close, a marker on the horizon, a service in the constellation).
Figures are instruments in the workspace bar, not rows of cards; one gold next step where the decision is made.
Explanations live in the review, not the product: about ten words a line inside the office.

diagnosis.title: ONE LAYOUT FOR EVERY KIND OF WORK
findings: Six different records (policy, repair, load, permit, deadline, factoring submission) share one header, one key-value table, one action column and one history list — on all 504 new pages.
Nothing in the composition says “this is a truck” or “this is a deadline”; meaning lives only in words.

diagnosis.title: VEHICLES & FLEET — THE TRUCK IS A TABLE
findings: The truck has no presence: a form of six fields.
Eight equal tiles — the out-of-service blocker looks like “0 documents”.
Actions are paragraphs in a side column; related work is squeezed into a narrow strip.
Phone: 1,945 px tall — 2.7 screens of scrolling.

diagnosis.title: BOOKKEEPING — A LIST WHERE A WORKBENCH SHOULD BE
findings: The nine-step close is a tall list.
The actual work — three questions — is one sentence.
A paragraph stands where the worktable belongs; history pushed below the fold.

diagnosis.title: COMPLIANCE — DEADLINES WITHOUT TIME
findings: A photo band repeated on every lane — decoration, not information.
Four stat tiles repeat the columns below them.
Due dates as lists, with no sense of time or urgency; three sections as empty hatched boxes.

diagnosis.title: CLIENT 360 — A CONTACT CARD, NOT A BUSINESS
findings: The title block pushes the work down.
Eight tabs of the same row template; the company is a form.
Services are a plain list — no sense of a connected business. Phone: 1,563 px.

rules.detail: No photo band on workspaces. A slim workspace bar (lane number, title, instruments, tools), then the work.
Three regions on desktop — a selector, a working stage, a context panel — shaped differently for each job.
At 1440 × 900 a workspace fits the screen; only lists scroll inside their region. No page scroll.
Show the state; reveal detail one section at a time in the context panel (a drawer on the phone).
Figures are condensed readouts in the bar (and they filter); never a row of repeated stat cards.
Every status is a shape and a word. Oxblood only for late or blocking; gold for selection and “now”.
One gold action where the decision is made. Simulated actions confirm inline and say SIMULATED — NOTHING IS SAVED OR SENT.
Copy budget inside the office; explanations live in the review, never in the product. Not-built states are one line.
Obsidian stages for focus (the truck, the client plate, the selected row), ivory surfaces to work on, gold for the path, hairlines for structure.
Photography identifies or sets place (the night yard behind the truck), never decorates a lane header.
Cross-workspace jumps keep a BACK TO … path and the selection they came from; Client 360 drills in and back without losing the company.
Phone, tablet, desktop and ultra-wide are each composed, not shrunk: strips and drawers on phone, stacked stage on tablet, full width on ultra-wide.
